D.t: Amy Klobuchar leads by 13.7 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 383,172 votes; a one point swing is about 13,944 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +6.6 and D +20.7. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +7.9. Your best recent poll is Mason-Dixon for the Star Tribune at D +9.8; your worst is co/efficient (R) at D +5.9. 5 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Hennepin, a projected net 339,549 votes; Ramsey, a projected net 136,185 votes; Dakota, a projected net 51,547 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Anoka, D +3.6, 6.3% of the vote; Scott, R +2.4, 2.7% of the vote; Carver, D +0.6, 2.1% of the vote; Rice, D +8.4, 1.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Amy Klobuchar runs furthest behind in Stearns, Sherburne, Wright. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 87% of voters, 52 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.37 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 55 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.76 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 60% of voters, 58 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.02 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Amy Klobuchar: Immigration voters 21 to 75, Small counties 37 to 59, Voters who can afford daily costs 48 to 48. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$3.5M cash against $618K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
